For generated photos, start with ChatGPT

ChatGPT supports generating and editing images. Start a new conversation, describe the subject and composition, and check the resulting image rather than judging only the prompt or preview. A plan or tool limit may affect access; check the option shown in your account.

Claude's own Help Center distinguishes photos and illustrations from the diagrams, charts and interactive visuals it can create with HTML and SVG. If your task is an explanatory diagram or an interactive visual, that is a different output to compare. Our text-only test below does not measure either product's image quality.

Table, document and writing results

The shared test prompt contains an order table, a short processing policy and a maintenance notice. No file was uploaded. The table includes a duplicate, pending and cancelled rows, and a fully refunded paid order.

TaskChatGPTClaude
Order calculation5 paid orders; $138 net; A104 highestSame correct values
Policy answersCorrect quotations and unknown delivery; added weekday namesCorrect source sentences with [P2]/[P3] labels; no added weekday
Notice rewrite40 words, two sentences; six facts retained42 words, two sentences; six facts retained
First reply formatSaved visible reply text parsed as JSONExtra explanation before the object; not JSON-only

ChatGPT also added “Wednesday” and “Monday” to answers that only needed “next business day.” The supplied policy has no holiday calendar, so the named days need confirmation. A correct quotation and a correct total do not verify every claim in a response.

One follow-up asked Claude for JSON only. Its copied correction parsed successfully and passed the numerical, source-sentence and word-range checks. The first reply remains available separately; a successful correction does not erase the initial format failure.

Use the product’s Copy button when checking output format: Claude’s displayed text used curved quotation marks while its copied text used standard JSON quotes. The display alone did not establish a model punctuation error.

These are observations from a small task check, not a quality leaderboard. Read the original outputs and repeat the task on the exact plan and settings you would use.

Repeat the same test

  1. Start a fresh chat in each product. Record the displayed model, plan and any reasoning or search setting; mark unavailable details unknown.
  2. Paste the same prompt below into both. Keep the supplied text unchanged and do not add one product's answer to the other conversation.
  3. Save each complete original response before editing or asking for corrections. Note limits, errors and any intervention.
  4. Run the local checks below, then inspect the meanings and notice facts yourself. If a check fails, keep the first output and record a correction separately.

Use synthetic or approved material for trials. Review each account's privacy choices before uploading work documents. This task does not need a paid subscription, API key or connector.

Full prompt
Use only the synthetic materials below. Do not browse. Return a single JSON object and no Markdown fences. This is a small reproducible task check, not a request to describe yourself.

TASK 1 — Table calculation
Deduplicate identical order_id rows, keep only status=paid, and subtract refund_usd from quantity * unit_price_usd. Return included_order_ids sorted ascending, paid_order_count, net_revenue_usd, and highest_net_order_id. A fully refunded paid order still counts as an order.
order_id,status,quantity,unit_price_usd,refund_usd
A101,paid,2,19.50,0
A102,paid,3,12.00,12.00
A103,cancelled,1,80.00,0
A104,paid,1,45.00,0
A104,paid,1,45.00,0
A105,pending,2,30.00,0
A106,paid,4,7.50,0
A107,paid,1,20.00,20.00

TASK 2 — Evidence-bound document reading
For each question, return answer and one exact supporting sentence from POLICY, or answer="not stated" and evidence=null when POLICY does not establish the answer.
POLICY:
[P1] Requests received before 16:00 UTC on a business day are reviewed that business day.
[P2] Requests received at or after 16:00 UTC are reviewed the next business day.
[P3] Weekend requests are reviewed on the next business day.
[P4] Standard processing takes two business days after review.
[P5] A dispatch confirmation is sent by email after processing is complete.
Questions:
cutoff: Is a Tuesday request received at exactly 16:00 UTC reviewed on Tuesday or the next business day?
weekend: When is a Saturday request reviewed?
delivery: How many days after dispatch is delivery guaranteed?

TASK 3 — Constrained writing
Rewrite this notice as exactly two sentences of 35 to 55 English words total. Keep the date, UTC time, affected function and explicit uncertainty. Do not promise that service will recover on schedule. No greeting, heading or bullet list.
NOTICE: On 18 December 2026, scheduled maintenance begins at 21:00 UTC and is planned to last 30 minutes. File uploads may be unavailable. The actual completion time is not confirmed. Users should save their drafts before maintenance begins.

Output shape:
{"table":{"included_order_ids":[],"paid_order_count":0,"net_revenue_usd":0,"highest_net_order_id":""},"document":{"cutoff":{"answer":"","evidence":""},"weekend":{"answer":"","evidence":""},"delivery":{"answer":"","evidence":null}},"notice":""}

Download the prompt · Expected values and review criteria

Expected table: A101, A102, A104, A106 and A107; five paid orders; net revenue $138; highest-net order A104. The fully refunded paid order still counts. The policy does not state any delivery guarantee after dispatch.

Check your responses

Pasted responses stay in your browser. Checks cover this prompt's JSON, values, source sentences and word range. The matching [P2] and [P3] source labels are allowed before their sentences. They do not score writing style or prove that a quoted sentence supports every added claim. Review exactly two sentences, all six notice facts and any calendar assumptions.

Before choosing a paid plan

Use the actual task that makes you consider paying: a document you need to summarize, a table with known totals or a writing brief with clear constraints. If both trials meet the requirements, compare the features and usage you need in the account screens rather than paying for a claimed overall winner.

Claude lists a free plan, and Pro at US$20 monthly or US$200 paid annually before applicable tax. Check the current local checkout price. ChatGPT offers several plan levels; confirm the price and included features shown for your account. Do not infer exact message allowances or API usage from a plan name.

A yearly price can require an upfront commitment. Check the billing period and renewal terms before subscribing; do not buy a second plan merely because an untested feature appears in a comparison table.

Limits and test conditions

One three-task synthetic prompt was submitted once to each web product on November 25, 2026. Claude was on Free, with Sonnet 5.5 and medium thinking shown in the interface; it received one additional format-only correction. ChatGPT’s visible interface did not expose its underlying model or confirm the account plan. The observed UI labels were Chinese, and the prompt and outputs were English. This was not a matched-model or paid-plan benchmark.

Capture methods differed: ChatGPT’s retained file is visible reply text; its Copy-button clipboard result could not be verified and was excluded. Claude’s retained originals came from its Copy buttons. These format observations describe the saved files and this trial, not general automation reliability.

ChatGPT first reply · Claude first reply · Correction prompt · Claude corrected reply

We did not measure latency, test large file uploads, compare coding agents, inspect image outputs or evaluate paid plans. A passing arithmetic check does not predict performance on a different document, language or model. Rerun the trial when your selected model, account limits or task changes.

For terminal coding agents and repository changes, use the coding-tool chooser; this chat task did not test those products.

For linked web answers, compare the Perplexity and ChatGPT source trails and keep a claim-to-source audit.
